script.title: How Vaccines Train the Immune System
script.topic: How vaccines train the immune system

scenes.narration: Did you know vaccination can train your immune system to fight more than just the disease it's designed for? This is called trained immunity, a new concept in immunology.
Trained immunity works by changing how our innate immune cells remember threats. These changes are often epigenetic, affecting gene expression without altering DNA.

This trained immunity can protect against unrelated infections, like the BCG vaccine reducing child mortality from other diseases. Studies show vaccinated mothers' children have lower disease risks, suggesting a transgenerational effect.
Vaccines are crucial for public health, preventing diseases like smallpox and polio. Getting vaccinated protects you and others through herd immunity.
